memory_bridge: A flying SHOE lands in the chosen player’s 手, retrieving シュ in 選手; when the shoe is removed, the hand itself is simply 手（て）.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 選手（せんしゅ）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The 選手（せんしゅ） catches a flying SHOE in one outstretched hand. SHOE closely retrieves On シュ in the word “player.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 手（て）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Remove the shoe and focus on the pictured hand itself: 手（て）. The standalone native noun is the complete anchor for Kun て.
